coachingPoints: Help from the ball side shoulder of your man, never from behind him
Stay low and active in help — standing straight up makes you a statue
Stunt early to slow the driver, then recover before your man catches the ball
Communicate every help action — 'I got help!' and 'recover!' keep the defense connected
The low man rotates to the roller; the weak side fills behind him
commonMistakes: Helping too deep and losing your own man for a kick-out three
Helping late — the driver is already at the rim by the time you arrive
Standing flat-footed in help with hands down and eyes only on the ball
Helping when your man is a dangerous shooter — know personnel
description: Help defense: when to leave your man, where to position yourself, and how to stop the drive without giving up open shots.

diagram.title: Help defender (X3) steps in to stop the drive

gameSituations: A teammate gets beaten off the dribble on the wing
A ball screen forces a switch or a drop and the guard turns the corner
A post player starts to back down your big
A baseline drive needs the low man to step across and take a charge or contest

howTo.detail: When your man is two or more passes away from the ball, move into a help position: inside the lane line, roughly level with the ball or a step below it. You guard space, not your man.
howTo.title: Get into help position off the ball

howTo.detail: Keep your head on a swivel: one eye on the ball, one eye on your man. The instant the ball handler beats his defender or the ball is driven toward you, you are the next line of defense.
howTo.title: Read the ball, feel your man

howTo.detail: Step toward the driving lane with your ball-side foot and hand, presenting a wall. Stop the ball first — worry about your own man second.
howTo.title: Step in to stop the ball

howTo.detail: Your job in help is to contain, not to steal. Make the driver pick up the ball, change direction, or throw a pass. A charge or a contested two beats a foul or an and-one.
howTo.title: Contain, don't gamble

howTo.detail: Once the ball is stopped or passed out, sprint back to your man under control. Recovery is part of the play — a late closeout after good help still gives up the shot.
howTo.title: Recover to your man

title: Help Defense
whatIsIt: Help defense is the team-wide principle that no defender guards alone. When the ball beats one defender, the nearest off-ball defenders rotate over to stop it — stepping into the driving lane, stunting at the driver, or fully rotating to take the charge or contest.

In a well-coached team, five defenders move as one connected unit: the ball is stopped by help, the helper's man is picked up by the next rotation, and everyone recovers. In a poorly connected team, help comes late or not at all, and one beaten defender becomes a layup.
The classic help rule: you are either guarding the ball or helping guard the ball. If your man is two passes away, your job is to be in position to stop a drive before it reaches the rim.
whyItMatters: No defender stays in front of the ball forever. Help defense is the insurance policy that makes man-to-man defense work at all. Teams with great help principles give up contested midrange shots; teams without them give up layups and open threes. Teaching help early is what turns five individual defenders into a defense.
